title: Get the parcel out of a locked curbside mailbox with its key, then shut and lock it and put the key back
instruction: Get the parcel out of the locked mailbox: unlock the access door with its key, take the parcel out and put it inside the taped rectangle on the table, then shut the access door, lock it, and put the key back on its mat.
context: This tests what key-in-lock tasks such as RoboDojo's insert_key do not: a working lock that gates a real door in a forced order, on a real mailbox (Architectural Mailboxes Oasis Classic 6200B-10). The plug turns only with the key fully home; turned, its cam clears the frame and the door, drawn past its magnet, falls open with the key riding in it; the door will not shut on a thrown cam, so it must be shut before the key is turned back; the key comes out only when locked. The parcel must come out through a 245 x 95 mm opening. Getting the mail is an everyday chore: about 40 percent of US delivery points are curbside (USPS OIG, RISC-WP-26-002), the Postal Inspection Service received over 800,000 mail theft complaints in FY2023-2025 (USPS OIG 25-137-R26), and carriers may not accept keys to private boxes (USPS POM 632.21), so unlocking, emptying and locking the box is the resident's job.
setup: Millimetres; x away from the robot (from the line through the arms' bases), y to its left, z up from the bench. An Architectural Mailboxes Oasis Classic 6200B-10 locking parcel mailbox (black powder-coated galvanized steel, 15.2 in tall, 12.0 wide, 18.1 deep, 22.44 lb, keyed cam lock, two keys) stands with its front face at x 320, centred at y 0, bolted through the maker's 4x4 adapter plate (item 7530) to a 35 mm cut of 4x4 post (89 x 89) screwed to a 300 x 260 x 19 plywood base clamped to the bench, its bottom 60 above the bench (a bench stand-in for its post). Its access door (265 x 105, hinged along its bottom edge, held shut by a magnet) is shut and locked, the key out; the lock's axis sits 22 mm in from the access opening's right edge. The hopper door (with its outgoing-mail clip) is shut and the flag down; they are part of the product and are not used in this task. Inside, on the floor of the box, lies the parcel: a ULINE S-425 White Indestructo Mailer (outside 4-3/4 x 3-3/8 x 2-3/8 in, 121 x 86 x 60, white corrugated) with a 200 g calibration weight taped inside (0.24 kg), lying on one of its 121 x 60 sides (60 across, 86 tall), its length front to back, its near end 12 behind the inside of the front panel, centred at y 50. The parcel's place is an outline of 24 mm blue painter's tape on the bench, 160 (x) by 100 (y) inside, centred at (235, 50). One of the box's keys lies flat on a 100 x 100 x 3 black silicone mat centred at (227, -255), its blade pointing away from the robot, its bow's centre at (215, -255). For scoring, two phones on tripods film the trial: one at the mailbox's front from the robot's left, one from above the bench.
scoring: 1.0: the 0.75 state, the key lying on its mat, everything still and both hands clear, held for 1 s. 0.75: the parcel on its place, and the access door shut and locked. 0.5: the parcel on its place. 0.25: the access door was opened by the key. 0: anything else, and for the rest of the trial once the key or the parcel has left the bench (its centre off the bench top, or its lowest point more than 50 mm below it). Every rung above 0 needs the door opened by the key: open more than 30 degrees while the plug was turned more than 45 degrees toward unlocked (a parcel got out any other way scores 0). The parcel on its place: seen from above, the rectangle that bounds it (sides parallel to the bench's edges) inside the tape's inside edges, and its lowest point within 6 mm of the bench; it may stand or lie on any face. Shut: the access door within 1.5 degrees of shut. Locked: the plug within 5 degrees of locked (the key's slot horizontal). The key on its mat: the rectangle that bounds it, seen from above, inside the mat's edges or at most 5 mm past them, and its lowest point within 6 mm of the mat's top. Still: every moving part (both doors, the plug, the key, the mail clip, the flag, the parcel) under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s. Hands clear: every point of both grippers' finger pads, and the point midway between them, at least 30 mm from the box (sides parallel to the bench's edges) that bounds each of those parts. Real trial: the video shows the door opened with the key's bow upright (turned) and the 1 s hold; a photo from above with the tape in view shows the parcel inside it and the key on its mat; a protractor app on a paused frame gives the door's angle; with the key out, the keyway's slot is horizontal at locked, and a luggage scale hooked on a loop of tape on the door's top edge, pulled outward to 5 N, does not open the door past 5 degrees; a ruler gives the hands' 30 mm.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes (an estimate, not timed); nothing is consumed. If the key is not on its mat, turn it to locked and take it out. Put the parcel back inside on its side at its marks (pencil lines on the floor of the box: its near end 12 mm behind the front panel, its centre 50 mm left of the box's centre line). Shut the access door and check it is locked (it does not open by hand). Shut the hopper door, flag down. Lay the key on its mat at its marks, blade pointing away from the robot. Before the first trial, break any burr on the access door's free edge and the lock's bezel with a file; nothing sharp, hot or wet touches the pads.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies at real size and mass. The keyway is a 2.6 x 8.5 mm slot for a 2.0 x 7.5 mm blade; a real lock fits its key far more closely, so insertion is easier here than on the real box. Rules, gated on real motion: the plug is held unless the key is fully home (then the blade's contact turns it, with a light snap at each end); the key is held in while the plug is turned; magnets hold each door within 3 degrees of shut. Not simulated: wafers, bitting, weather strip.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (all 4,000 steps; the access door stays shut and nothing is seen picked up); demo: 1.0 on 3 of 3 trials on one GPU type (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000; each trial ends on success after 1,981 control steps)
